messages.author: f1a78b77bed56547
messages.subject: browser() print() in renderPlot({})
parts:
Hi,

For debugging. I am running local using Rstudio. I placed a browser() call inside a renderPlot({}). When the code runs it interupts and offers an R prompt as expected. However, when I try to print a value, I can't 'see' it. I have resorted to writing the value to a file, but this is a huge headache for on the fly debuggin. How may I turn on display of the value?

Example code:

output$graph <- renderPlot({
   a = 1
   browser()
})

Example run:

> runApp()

Listening on http://127.0.0.1:5970
Browse[1]> a
Browse[1]> print(a)
Browse[1]> 

Notice that in response to typing 'a' at the prompt, and in response to typing 'print(a)' at the prompt there is no displayed output.

It seems that in the context of a renderPlot({}) the console display is turned off. How may I turn it back on?

Jonathan

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: browser() print() in renderPlot({})
parts:
You can use sink() to get the console back, although it may interfere with display of graphics sent to the browser.

This is an issue that's in 0.10.0, but it's been fixed in 0.10.1, which is on CRAN now (the binary package for Mac OS X 10.9 isn't up yet but should be soon).

-WInston

messages.subject: Re: browser() print() in renderPlot({})
parts:
Since the shiny package is a pure R package (no C/C++/Fortran code), I
think it should be installable on all platforms just from the source
package, i.e.

install.packages('shiny', type = 'source', repos = 'http://cran.rstudio.com')

It is only the Mavericks binaries that are not ready yet for some
reason. Windows/Snow Leopard binaries have been there for a few days.

Regards,
Yihui
